title: Redwood PLG Quickstart Discovery - Harbor Systems
summary: Discovery call focused on quickstart experience and tradeoffs between Redwood hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Harbor is evaluating for chat/assistant and embeddings for search; primary concerns are data residency, PII handling, and predictable latency for user-facing product. Discussed free credits / trial, SDK quickstart, timing to first token, and next steps to run a small benchmark and share security docs.
action_items: Alex - send PLG quickstart link and sample cURL + SDK snippet - 2026-09-02
Priya - share benchmark checklist and suggested models for 8k context summary test - 2026-09-04
Jules - confirm data residency/SaaS policy and share internal requirements doc - 2026-09-03
next_steps: Redwood to provide quickstart credits and onboarding steps (free credits)
Schedule a 60-min technical deep dive with infra team next week (SE-led)
Customer to run a 1k-5k message pilot and share perf results
header:
Date: 2026-09-01
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Desai (Redwood SE); Mark Holt (Harbor CTO); Sara Kim (Lead ML Eng); Chris Rivera (Product); Jules (Data Privacy)
Recording link: https://app.fireflies.ai/recordings/ff-2026-09-01-harbor-001
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, i'll kick off. how's the audio?
[00:08] Mark Holt: Good here, can you hear me.
[00:12] Priya Desai: Yup, all good. quick agenda: run through Harbor's use case, current infra, show how fast you can get started with our PLG quickstart and credit offer, then dive into hosting options.
[00:28] Chris Rivera: We're mostly interested in an assistant for our support workflow and embeddings for semantic search. primary constraints: PII, latency under 400ms for short chats, and cost at scale.
[00:45] Alex Chen: Great, that's helpful. Mark, what are you using today?
[00:51] Mark Holt: Right now we use OpenAI via API for prototyping, and an internal vector store on AWS. support volume is ramping, costs are spiking, and egress is a pain with our EU customers. also need SSO and audit logs for compliance.
[01:10] Sara Kim: We also have batch offline embeddings jobs on SageMaker for indexing, but they'd like embeddings near real-time.
[01:18] Priya Desai: ok so a few things we usually help with: quickstart path to first token (we provide free credits to spin up), model recommendations for cost/latency, and options to move to Dedicated or Private when you need VPC or on-prem.
[01:34] Mark Holt: How fast is first token? like realistic time to get from signup to sending a call?
[01:40] Alex Chen: For PLG hosted API, most teams get to first token in under 10 minutes if they follow the quickstart — sign up, create API key, run cURL or the SDK. we'll share snippets.
[01:52] Chris Rivera: And free credits?
[01:54] Alex Chen: Yes we can issue trial credits tied to the account, enough to run a small pilot — usually a couple hundred dollars equivalent.
[02:03] Sara Kim: On security: does Redwood offer SAML SSO and KMS? we need customer-managed keys for sensitive PII.
[02:12] Priya Desai: For Hosted we support SSO integrations and encryption at rest. Customer-managed KMS is available on Private and Dedicated with our enterprise plans; Hosted can use server-side managed keys but we have feature tiers. Jules, do you have specific compliance requirements?
[02:26] Jules: We need SOC 2 plus evidence of audit logs, and we have a list of data retention and data residency requirements for EU customers. also want to understand where logs show up and who can see them.
[02:38] Alex Chen: We can share our security pack — SOC 2 report, data flow diagrams, and audit log examples. we'll redact sensitive bits. I'll send that after the call.
[02:48] Mark Holt: On latency: you mentioned dedicated pools? what's the difference in p95 between hosted and dedicated generally?
[02:56] Priya Desai: Good q. Hosted is multi-tenant so p95 can vary based on load but we optimize with continuous batching and KV caching. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and more predictable p95; typical difference is hosted p95 ~ 200-600ms for short chat requests depending on model, dedicated can be consistently lower and you can tune batching and kernel selection. numbers depend on model size and quantization.
[03:20] Sara Kim: What about model variants — can we fall back to cheaper models for non-sensitive queries to save cost?
[03:25] Alex Chen: Absolutely. Smart routing lets you route by policy — latency tier, cost tier, region; automatic fallback to a compatible lighter-weight variant is supported.
[03:33] Chris Rivera: Any friction to integrate with our vector db? we use an in-house vector service and Postgres for metadata.
[03:39] Priya Desai: No problem, embeddings are standard REST calls; we provide SDK helpers for common vector stores; also support webhooks and async jobs for bulk embeddings.
[03:50] Mark Holt: For Private deployment, what's the timeline and effort? we might need VPC with internal-only control plane.
[03:58] Priya Desai: Private is typically a few weeks for onboarding depending on infra; we have an on-prem package for air-gapped setups. VPC Private includes customer-managed network and can integrate with your KMS/HSM. Dedicated is faster — days to a couple weeks — and gives reserved capacity without full private control plane.
[04:18] Jules: Cost question: if we start hosted PLG then move to Dedicated, do tokens transfer or do we have to reconfigure?
[04:24] Alex Chen: You can pin model versions and redirect traffic; billing and quotas differ but we help migrate keys and configs. We'll provide a migration playbook.
[04:33] Mark Holt: Any rate limiting or quotas during quickstart? we don't want to hit soft-limits mid-pilot.
[04:38] Alex Chen: We'll set pilot quotas and can temporarily raise limits. For production we discuss committed capacity for Dedicated.
[04:44] Chris Rivera: About the quickstart, can we get a sample cURL and a JS SDK snippet now?
[04:48] Alex Chen: Sure. I'll paste links after the call but briefly: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <api_key>" -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-medium","input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate. JS SDK is one-liner to init with key and call chat.
[05:05] Sara Kim: You mentioned KV cache earlier — can you expand? we cache user conversation context server-side right?
[05:11] Priya Desai: yes KV caching stores prefix key value cache to avoid re-encoding the whole conversation; helps reduce latency and cost. sometimes the transcript shows as "K V cash" in older notes but it's KV cache.
[05:23] Mark Holt: Performance testing — we'd like to run a 1k-message test and measure p50/p95 and token cost. what's the best way to do that?
[05:31] Priya Desai: We'll share a bench checklist: sample payloads, synthetic concurrency, and a small harness you can run. We'll also propose 3 model configs: small low-latency, medium cost/quality, and large high-quality.
[05:45] Chris Rivera: Do you have an example of billing breakdown at token level?
[05:49] Alex Chen: Yes console shows token-level cost per route/model and latency breakdown; we can export CSVs.
[05:55] Jules: For EU data residency — can Hosted guarantee EU-only region?
[05:59] Priya Desai: Hosted has regional endpoints; we can provision EU-only tenancy for enterprise customers but for strict residency we usually recommend Private.
[06:09] Mark Holt: Who typically owns rollout on your side for Dedicated/Private? is it the SE or customer success?
[06:15] Alex Chen: SE owns the technical onboarding, Customer Success owns the account-level rollout and SLA, and Solutions Eng helps with benchmark/optimization.
[06:23] Sara Kim: Any gotchas with streaming? we rely on streaming tokens to show immediate assistant responses.
[06:27] Priya Desai: Streaming supported out of the box; pay attention to connection timeouts and chunk sizes. We'll share best-practice config for web clients.
[06:35] Mark Holt: Ok let's talk timeline — we want to pilot in two weeks and decide in six weeks for a potential Dedicated commit.
[06:44] Alex Chen: Sounds reasonable. We'll grant free quickstart credits today, send quickstart + SDK snippets, security pack, and schedule a technical deep dive early next week.
[06:55] Chris Rivera: One more thing: any references or case studies for comparable customers in regulated spaces?
[06:59] Alex Chen: Yes we have case studies and a reference list; I'll include one for a FinTech and a HealthTech customer who did similar migration to Dedicated.
[07:10] Mark Holt: Nice. that's it from us, thanks.
[07:13] Alex Chen: Great—recap: Alex send quickstart + credits + security docs; Priya send benchmark checklist; Jules confirm residency requirements. will follow up with calendar invite for deep dive. Thanks everyone.
[07:25] End of recording
